title: VisionQuest Doubles Down on Scarlet Witch's Death as Wanda Maximoff Fate Confirmed | Entertainment
text:
VisionQuest confirms Scarlet Witch's death in Doctor Strange 2, as Vision reveals Wanda Maximoff was crushed under Mount Wundagore, sparking new debate.
In the new Marvel series VisionQuest, the fate of Wanda Maximoff, also known as the Scarlet Witch, appears to be confirmed. During the premiere of the series, Vision states that Wanda was crushed under the weight of a mountain, referring to the collapse of Mount Wundagore in the 2022 film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. This admission comes four years after the character's apparent death, and it doubles down on the idea that Wanda is truly gone.
Background on Scarlet Witch's Fate
At the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Wanda Maximoff sacrifices herself by destroying every copy of the Darkhold and bringing Mount Wundagore crashing down around her. No body was shown, leading many fans to hope that the Scarlet Witch might return. However, the 2024 series Agatha All Along supported the idea that Wanda is dead, as her demise freed Agatha Harkness from a spell Wanda had cast in 2021's WandaVision. Now, VisionQuest has further solidified this fate.
VisionQuest is the third MCU series concluding a trilogy that includes WandaVision and Agatha All Along. In the new series, the rebuilt Vision attempts to understand his identity and form a connection to the memories and humanity of his past self. Wanda's complicated legacy and fate remain extremely relevant to the show in more ways than one. The series also brings back Paul Bettany's Vision and James Spader's Ultron.
VisionQuest Confirms Wanda's Death
In the premiere of VisionQuest, Vision confirms that Wanda was crushed under the weight of a mountain. This reference to the collapse of Mount Wundagore feels pretty cut and dry rather than some sort of unresolved MCU mystery. While this isn't to say that there couldn't perhaps be a future reveal that brings a being as magically powerful as Wanda Maximoff back to the land of the living, her fate currently feels pretty black and white. Likewise, it's a pretty disappointing conclusion considering just how controversial Wanda's last appearance was.
The MCU has an established track record of reversing apparent deaths, either by featuring characters from other timelines or realities or full-on resurrections. Case in point, both Vision and Ultron are back in VisionQuest. However, Wanda's fate seems more definitive this time. The admission in VisionQuest makes Wanda's death even more controversial than it already was.
Impact on Scarlet Witch's Story
Four years later, Marvel proves that Scarlet Witch's villain turn makes no sense. The frustrating irony of Wanda Maximoff's death was that it was the direct consequence of her attempts to redeem the darkness and damage she caused as the primary antagonist of Multiverse of Madness, desperate to reunite with her twin boys Billy and Tommy in another reality no matter the cost. Thanks to Doctor Strange and America Chavez, Wanda ultimately understood how dark she had become, explaining her sacrifice by the movie's end.
However, her entire villain turn has become completely unnecessary four years later. Both Agatha All Along and VisionQuest have since revealed that Wanda's children made their way back into the main MCU timeline anyway, thanks to Billy's magic placing his and Tommy's souls into the bodies of teens William Kaplan and Thomas Shepard before Wanda removed her Hex over Westview. As seen by the end of VisionQuest's first two episodes, Thomas and Vision have now found each other, and the end of Agatha All Along confirmed that Billy had begun searching for his brother.
As such, the MCU looks to be gearing up for a full reunion of the surviving members of the Maximoff family, making Wanda's dark turn post-WandaVision even more frustrating, while also making a potential resurrection feel even more necessary to make up for it. Basically, Wanda Maximoff corrupted herself trying to reach her children, only for both boys to return without her needing to rewrite reality to begin with. While Wanda couldn't have known this would happen, her actions still had devastating consequences.
Keeping all of this in mind, if any MCU character deserves to be brought back, it's Wanda Maximoff's Scarlet Witch, who clearly deserves so much more than the unnecessary fate she was given. New episodes of VisionQuest release Tuesday nights on Disney+ from Marvel Studios.
